description:
FILED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07) from #1061's CPAN-board bisects.

perl's `use overload …` is a BEGIN: the handler table is installed while the
file COMPILES, so it is in force for every run-time statement of that file
wherever the `use` sits.  PCL emits `(p-register-overloads "Foo" …)` at the
statement's RUN position (Pl/Parser.pm::_process_use_overload), and
Pl/Parser2.pm's section assembly deliberately leaves `use`/`require`/BEGIN
statements IN the statement stream ("position matters: a module must load
before the code that follows it runs").

Before s436's phase model that was invisible in a single-section file --
source order was run order.  Since `b95ad912` every SECTION's compile phase
runs before every section's RUN phase, so a trailing `{ package Foo; use
overload …; sub new {…} }` block has its `sub new` available to earlier code
(good, and perl-correct) while its overload table is still installed AFTER
that code has run.  The two halves of one `use` now disagree.

REPRODUCER (perl prints 3/3/1; PCL prints the object's default
stringification):

    use List::Util qw(max min);
    my ($one,$two,$thr) = (Foo->new(1), Foo->new(2), Foo->new(3));
    print max($one,$two,$thr), "\n";      # perl 3   PCL Foo=SCALAR(0x3)
    print min($one,$two,$thr), "\n";      # perl 1   PCL Foo=SCALAR(0x1)
    { package Foo;
      use overload '""' => sub { ${$_[0]} }, '0+' => sub { ${$_[0]} },
                   '>'  => sub { ${$_[0]} > ${$_[1]} }, fallback => 1;
      sub new { my $c = shift; my $v = shift; bless \$v, $c } }

Move the `{ package Foo; … }` block ABOVE the prints and PCL agrees with perl
on every line -- that is the whole difference.

BOARD COST.  Scalar-List-Utils max.t / min.t / product.t (and sum.t, sum0.t,
… -- the whole List::Util t/ family writes the class after its first use)
went PASS -> PARTIAL at `b95ad912`: the phase model made `Foo->new` work, so
rows 6 and 7 (`is($v, 3, 'overload')`) RUN for the first time and fail on the
missing `""` handler.  MORE coverage, honest failures -- but the failures are
this bug.

FIX SHAPE (not designed here).  `p-register-overloads` belongs in the
section's COMPILE phase, next to the `@{ $sec->{captured} }` forms, not in
`$sec->{run}`.  The handlers are closures over nothing (they are `sub {…}`
literals in the pragma's own argument list) in every spelling seen so far, so
hoisting looks safe -- but a handler naming a file lexical would then be
compiled above its `p-defcell`, which is exactly the hazard the phase model's
own comment records ("NOT hoist the definition alone ... Whole compile phase
or nothing", ruled s433).  Measure that shape before moving anything.

=== DONE (s473w, 2026-09-09) ===

SHIPPED, and the MEASUREMENT the task asked for came out the way the task
guessed: a `use overload` statement is a compile-phase member like a sub
definition, so the fix is the CLASSIFIER ARM, not a hoist of the registration.

WHERE: every `PPI::Statement::Include` already goes through Parser2's
`sched => 1` route (`Pl/Parser2.pm` ~9286), whose `definitions` bucket is where
a BEGIN block's `p-BEGIN` lands and which the #55 assembly interleaves with the
sub definitions BY SOURCE POSITION.  `Pl::Parser::_process_use_overload` now
emits into that bucket through the existing `_with_bucket('definitions', â¦)`
mechanism â three lines of change â so the registration happens exactly where a
BEGIN block written in its place would happen.  No new machinery, and s433's
"whole compile phase or nothing" holds because the whole statement moves.

THE HAZARD PROBED, and perl's own answer is not the naive one:

  handler closes over a FILE lexical assigned ABOVE the block
      perl a-5 / a-7      PCL before: Foo=SCALAR(0x1) / a-7   after: identical
  handler closes over a lexical declared INSIDE the class's own block
      perl 5 / T7 / T (perl warns "uninitialized" â `my $tag = "T"` is a
      RUN-time assignment, so a call made ABOVE the block sees undef)
      PCL before: Foo=SCALAR(0x1) / T7 / T   after: identical to perl
  two overloaded packages below their first use, a handler naming a sub
  defined LATER, overload::StrVal, overload::Overloaded
      perl 1a:A<3> 1b:B<4> / 2:C<9> / 3:raw / 4:yes
      PCL before: A=SCALAR(0x1) â¦ / 4:no     after: identical
  `use overload` inside a string eval: worked before and after (no regression)
  `no overload '0+'`: still ignored â PRE-EXISTING, identical on 0ece3088,
      filed as #1569

BARS.  corpus-diff vs `0ece3088`: 13 of 111 files differ, and all 13 are
exactly the files with a LIVE `use overload`; the other three that mention it
(a comment in concat.t, a handler-less `use overload;` in hexfp.t, a heredoc in
eval.t) are byte-identical.  Five sampled diffs are 42 lines, every one a moved
`p-register-overloads` form or its comment.  emission-ab over lib/ +
cpan-tests + the 14-dist board t/ (613 files): SAME 600 / DIFF 13 / RCDIFF 0.
Generation v2-1200, three artifacts regenerated, ir-host-leak identical (31
symbols over 111 files).  Guard `Pl/t/overload-01.t` 40 â 45 rows, four
inverse-verified on a `0ece3088` extraction.  ir-spec Â§the phase model names
the registration as a compile-phase member.  Commit `4bdde171`.
subject: `use overload` is a RUN-phase statement, but perl's `use` is a BEGIN: an overloaded class defined in a block LATER in the file has no `""`/`0+`/`>` handlers while earlier run-time code uses its objects (Scalar-List-Utils max.t/min.t/product.t rows 6-7, the shape every List::Util t-file uses)
